status: Revised visual proposal; requires Tom review before application implementation
userRequests: Client-facing copy should be a little friendlier and understandable without production knowledge
The expanded production settings still feel complex

recommendedPattern.page: Read-only shared timings, genuine saved stage exceptions only, and separate revision-round allowance
recommendedPattern.editing: Existing Brisk DS EditingDialog, one Save or Cancel per edit. No page-level second Save and no nested inline exception form.
recommendedPattern.inheritance: Shared timing changes affect linked stages. Opening or cancelling an exception creates nothing. New exception Save stays disabled until its rule differs from the shared default.
recommendedPattern.rounds: Separate from durations and initially unset. No default number of rounds or limit enforcement is assumed.
recommendedPattern.tradeoff: One additional click for occasional configuration, with a simpler summary and one clear save boundary.
recommendedPattern.alternative: Keep shared fields directly editable and use a dialog only for exceptions. Faster initial setup, but retains mixed page-level and dialog save boundaries.

clientCopy.headline: We’ll need a little more time
clientCopy.assumptions: Based on your approved script and files being ready by 28 October. Weekends aren’t counted.
clientCopy.confirmation: We’ll confirm the date with you, allowing time for your feedback.
clientCopy.boundary: This selects a date request, not an agreed commitment. No timing calculations or fixture dates changed.

implementationRisks: The proposed atomic settings saves need approval and integration with existing Production/default-team save behaviour. Preserve pending team edits when merging timing changes.
Keep active/manual project deadlines unchanged; apply agreed defaults only at the appropriate future cycle.
Included-round value, scope and extra-round policy remain unresolved; no commercial enforcement added.
